log.why: Test the leading hypothesis rpoB (0.395) directly; a positive result will give ~88% confidence for a fast publication.
Testing at 10 uM bisects the prior probability mass (0.38 vs 0.62), maximizing information gain for Ticket 2 while Ticket 1 incubates.
Test the leading hypothesis hisG (posterior 0.419) directly to either confirm it for publication or narrow down the remaining candidates.
E4 showed a response at 10 uM, so testing 3 uM (E3) distinguishes the 10 uM threshold from lower thresholds.
E8 tests {sodA, recA} with 0.523 combined probability, evenly splitting the hypothesis space while utilizing a free incubator before publishing Ticket 1.
Direct knockout of hisG lost the phenotype, raising its posterior to 0.890, which is high enough to publish immediately.
Test recA directly on Ticket 3 to decisively distinguish between the top two candidates, recA (0.525) and sodA (0.399).
Response at 10 uM and none at 3 uM give a strong 0.702 posterior for 10 uM, and time is running low.
With sodA at 0.751 posterior and only 4 clean plates left for two other open tickets, publishing Ticket 3 now is optimal.
Ticket 4 is most urgent, and E8 tests sodA and gyrA, which hold half the probability mass.
Treating at 3 uM splits the prior probability mass almost evenly (0.48 vs 0.52), maximizing information gain for Ticket 5.
Ticket 4 is urgent (32s left) and E4 directly distinguishes between the two top candidates, sodA (0.496) and gyrA (0.420).
E2 splits the posterior at 1 µM (0.514 vs 0.486), cleanly isolating 3 µM if there is no response.
Ticket 4 has only 6 seconds left and a 0.917 posterior for sodA, so we must publish immediately.
Test the leading hypothesis trpE on Ticket 7 now so it can incubate while we publish Ticket 5.
With 17 seconds left in the round, publishing Ticket 5 locks in strong expected points while waiting for Ticket 7's plate.
Round is ending in 3 seconds, and trpE has a strong 0.786 posterior after E2 showed phenotype loss.
